mainTopic: Does טבילה need כוונה for חולין versus מעשר, when may a person decide what his טבילה is for, and רבי יהודה's view that a foot still in the water counts as being in the מקוה.
overview: The amud opens with the end of an answer: when a person immerses for חולין, no כוונה is needed, but for מעשר it is. The גמרא tries to prove the חולין rule from a wave that falls on a person and on כלים. That proof is pushed off, so it brings a better proof from fruit that fell into a water channel. רבה then challenges רב נחמן twice from the wording of our משנה. רב נחמן answers both times, and a ברייתא backs him up. רבי אלעזר teaches that a person may choose his level of purity even after coming up from the water. A ברייתא about one foot still in the water is explained so that it fits his view, and רבי פדת says that ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. Two versions of רבה בר אבוה's statement disagree about where רבי יהודה's leniency applies. Finally, עולא asks whether רבי יהודה holds גוד אסיק. רבי יוחנן answers from the case of three pools in a stream, and a challenge from another ברייתא begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the answer: the other ברייתא is about מעשר
steps.stepSummary: This line finishes an earlier answer: the ברייתא that requires intention is talking about מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, the ברייתא is talking about מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the closing words of an answer from just before this section. The גמרא settled two ברייתות that seemed to clash by saying one is about חולין and this one is about מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One ברייתא says a person must have כוונה when he immerses, and another says he need not. The answer splits them: for חולין no כוונה is needed, but for מעשר, which is holier, כוונה is needed. This sets up the next question: how do we know חולין needs no כוונה?

keyTerms.meaning: Tithe; produce with a level of holiness, so its purity rules are stricter
Here, meaning in this ברייתא

phrases.english: here, it is for tithes.
phrases.notes: "Here" means the ברייתא that says intention is needed. This finishes the answer that started just before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a resolution that began on the earlier part of the daf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: חולין versus מעשר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to argue about whether טבילה needs כוונה.
steps.terutzMaskana: For מעשר כוונה is needed; for חולין it is not.

steps.title: What is the source that חולין needs no intention?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that immersing for חולין does not need כוונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do you know that חולין does not need intention?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for the half of the answer that says חולין needs no כוונה. This question sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 1 assumed that חולין needs no כוונה. Now the גמרא wants to see that this is actually taught somewhere, and is not just made up to settle the clash.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you say this? (asking for a source)
Ordinary food that is not holy
Intention, here meaning intending to become טהור
Need, require

phrases.english: And from where do you say
that non-sacred food does not require intention?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a source for the חולין half of the previous answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that טבילה for חולין works without כוונה.

steps.title: Proof from a wave that falls on a person and on כלים
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says a detached wave of forty סאה makes a person and כלים טהור. Since כלים cannot intend, the person here did not intend either.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the משנה teaches: if a wave with forty סאה broke off and fell on a person and on כלים, they are טהור. The משנה puts the person together with the כלים. Just as כלים have no intention, the person here also had no intention.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה about a wave to prove that a person can become טהור for חולין without any intention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works by comparing the two items the משנה lists side by side. כלים obviously cannot intend anything, so the person listed next to them must also be someone who was not thinking about טבילה. If he still becomes טהור, then כוונה is not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A wave that broke off from the sea
Forty סאה, the amount of water a מקוה needs
Similar to; the two cases are compared to each other
They intend

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna: a wave that became detached
and it contains forty se'a,
and it fell on a person and on vessels —
they are pure.
It teaches a person similar to vessels:
just as vessels do not intend —
so too a person who does not intend.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 with a proof from a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That טבילה for חולין works without כוונה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a detached wave that falls on a person and on כלים, read as the person being like the כלים.

steps.title: Maybe the משנה is about someone waiting for the wave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the proof: maybe the משנה is about someone sitting and waiting for the wave, so the comparison goes the other way.
steps.simpleTranslation: But how do you know? Maybe the משנה is about someone sitting and waiting for the wave to break off. Then the כלים are like the person: just as a person can intend, the כלים here are a case where someone intends for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by reading the משנה differently. Maybe there was intention after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof compared the person to the כלים. The גמרא flips it and compares the כלים to the person. If the person was waiting on purpose, then the owner also wanted the כלים to be purified, so intention was present for both. Now the משנה proves nothing about טבילה without כוונה.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where is that clear? (pushes back on a proof)
Perhaps
Sitting and waiting, meaning he wants this to happen
We are dealing with

steps.confusionAlert: Both readings use the same word דומיא, "similar to." The whole argument is about which side is compared to which: is the person like the כלים, or are the כלים like the person?

phrases.english: And from where is this clear?
Perhaps it is about one who sits and waits
for when the wave will detach, that we are dealing with,
and vessels are similar to a person:
just as a person is capable of intention —
so too vessels for which he intends.
phrases.notes: "He" is the owner. He is waiting for the wave and wants it to purify his כלים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 3 by reading the משנה another way.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof itself. It does not say that חולין needs כוונה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the person is like the כלים. It could just as well be that the כלים are like the person, so intention was there.

steps.title: If he was waiting, what does the משנה add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the משנה is about someone waiting with intention, what new thing would it be teaching?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the משנה is about someone sitting and waiting, why would it need to say that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading. If the person intended, it seems obvious that he becomes טהור, so why would the משנה bother to teach it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה is expected to teach something new. Forty סאה of water plus intention sounds like a plain טבילה. So the reading from step 4 seems to leave the משנה with nothing to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say
What is there to say? This seems obvious

phrases.english: And if you would say it is about one who sits and waits,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא בְּיוֹשֵׁב וּמְצַפֶּה, מַאי לְמֵימְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading offered in the דחיה of step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the משנה is about someone sitting and waiting.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If intention is present, the ruling seems obvious, and a משנה would not teach something obvious.

steps.title: The new point: no גזירה against a wave
steps.stepSummary: The משנה still teaches something new. We might have made a גזירה against a wave because of flowing rainwater, or because of the arcs of the wave. The משנה teaches that there is no such גזירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: let us make a גזירה, because someone might come to immerse in a flowing stream of rainwater. Or: let us make a גזירה against the edges of the wave because of its arcs. The משנה teaches us that we do not make these גזירות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the waiting reading by showing the משנה still has something new to teach. Even with intention, we might have thought a wave does not work because of a rabbinic גזירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is not about intention. It is that a wave is a valid מקוה, and the חכמים did not forbid it. One possible worry was that people would confuse it with flowing rainwater, which does not purify. The other was that people would confuse its edges, which touch the ground, with its arcs in the air. Since the משנה still teaches something, the reading from step 4 stands, and the proof for חולין is not accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: It would have entered your mind to say (the mistaken first thought)
Let us make a rabbinic גזירה (protective decree)
A flowing stream of rainwater
The edges of the wave because of its arcs
It teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the wave was pushed off. The משנה may be about someone who intended, and its new point is only that there is no גזירה against immersing in a wave. So this משנה does not prove that חולין needs no כוונה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common pattern in the גמרא: a proof falls away once we find a different חידוש, a new point, that the source could be teaching.

phrases.english: It would enter your mind to say:
let us decree, lest he come
to immerse in a flowing stream of rainwater,
phrases.notes: Rainwater only purifies when it is gathered in one place, not while it is still flowing.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי נִגְזוֹר רָאשִׁין אַטּוּ כִּיפִּין,
phrases.english: alternatively, let us decree the edges because of the arcs,
phrases.notes: The edges are the parts of the wave touching the ground. The arcs are the curved tops up in the air.

phrases.english: it teaches us that we do not decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 and keeps the reading of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finding a different new point: no rabbinic גזירה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have made a גזירה against a wave because of flowing rainwater or because of the arcs of the wave.
steps.terutzMaskana: No such גזירה exists, so the משנה teaches something even if the person intended.

steps.title: A source that you cannot immerse in the arc of a wave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know you cannot immerse under the arc of a wave. It answers with a ברייתא: you may immerse in the edges of waves but not in their arcs, because you cannot immerse in air.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that you cannot immerse in the arcs of a wave? A ברייתא teaches: you may immerse in the edges of waves, but not in their arcs, because you cannot immerse in the air.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to give a source for something it assumed in step 6: that immersing under a wave's arc does not work. It quotes a ברייתא that says so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6 the גמרא said we might have banned immersing in a wave because of its arcs. Here it proves the arcs really are a problem. The hollow space under a curling wave counts as air, not water, even if water surrounds the person on every side.

keyTerms.meaning: The arcs of a wave, where it curls over and leaves a hollow space underneath
The edges or ends of a wave, where the water is solid
Air. Here it means the empty space under the wave's arc
We immerse (a person or כלים in order to make them טהור)

phrases.english: And from where do you say
that one may not immerse in the arcs?
phrases.notes: This is the arc the גמרא mentioned in step 6, the curl of the wave.

phrases.english: As it is taught: One may immerse in the edges,
but one may not immerse in the arcs,
because one may not immerse in air.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a source for the 'arcs' concern that step 6 used to explain why the משנה about the wave still teaches something new.
steps.raayaObject: That immersing under the arc of a wave does not work
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: one may immerse in the edges of waves but not in their arcs, because one cannot immerse in air

steps.title: A new proof from fruit that fell into a water channel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the wave proof and brings a new one. A משנה in מכשירין says that a person with טמא hands who reaches into a water channel to take out fruit ends up with pure hands, even though he never meant to wash them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the proof comes from a משנה: If fruit fell into a water channel, and a person whose hands were טמא reached in and took the fruit out, his hands are טהור. The fruit is not under the rule of 'כי יותן'. But if he reached in so that his hands would get washed, his hands are טהור, and the fruit is under the rule of 'כי יותן'.
steps.whatsHappening: The wave proof fell apart, so the גמרא brings a brand-new proof that immersing for חולין does not need כוונה. In this משנה, a man's hands become pure even when he only meant to grab fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man in the first case wanted only to pick up the fruit, yet the משנה says his hands are טהור. So purity for חולין works without כוונה. His intention matters only for the fruit: if he wanted the water on his hands, the fruit becomes able to receive טומאה through the rule of 'כי יותן'.

keyTerms.meaning: A water channel (a stream of water that counts for purifying hands)
'If water be put on' (ויקרא 11:38). Food can become טמא only after it has been wet with water in a way the owner wanted
So that his hands would be rinsed (washed)
He stretched out (his hands)

steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the main proof that purity for חולין does not need כוונה. That is the very point רבה is about to challenge.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two results. The hands are טהור in BOTH cases. Only the fruit's status depends on what the man intended.

phrases.english: Rather, from that which we learned:
Fruit that fell into a water channel,
and one whose hands were impure stretched out and took them —
phrases.notes: He reached in only to get the fruit out, not to wash his hands.

phrases.english: his hands are pure,
and the fruit is not in the category of 'if water be put.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:38. The fruit got wet without anyone wanting it wet, so it still cannot become טמא.

phrases.english: And if it was in order that his hands be rinsed —
his hands are pure,
and the fruit is in the category of 'if water be put.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the wave proof, which was pushed off in step 4, with a new proof for the question asked in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That immersing or washing for חולין does not need כוונה
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה מכשירין: a person who reaches into a water channel only to take out fruit still ends up with טהור hands

steps.title: רבה challenges רב נחמן from the wording of our משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבה challenges רב נחמן using our משנה. It says that one who immersed for חולין 'and was considered pure for חולין' may still not eat מעשר. The words 'was considered pure' suggest that he only gets that status if he meant to.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה raised an objection to רב נחמן: Someone who immersed for חולין and was considered pure for חולין is still forbidden to eat מעשר. We can learn from this: if he was considered pure (because he intended it), yes, he has that status. If he was not considered pure in that way, no, he does not!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה attacks the view that immersing for חולין needs no כוונה. He reads an inference out of the wording of our own משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה adds the words 'והוחזק לחולין,' meaning he set himself up as pure for חולין. רבה reads this as showing that the status comes only when he intended it. If so, even חולין needs כוונה, which goes against רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: He was set up as, or considered to have, a status (here, pure for חולין)
Tithes, which need a higher level of purity than חולין
Yes (Aramaic)

steps.whyThisMatters: If רבה's inference holds, the rule that חולין needs no כוונה falls. The גמרא will now have to answer him.

phrases.english: Rabba raised an objection to Rav Nachman:
One who immersed for non-sacred food and was considered pure for non-sacred food —
phrases.notes: These are the words of our משנה, quoted on the previous amud.

phrases.english: is forbidden to eat tithes.
If he was considered pure, yes,
phrases.notes: He means: if he immersed intending to take on that status, then he has it.

phrases.english: if he was not considered pure, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof in step 8, רבה challenges the same rule (חולין needs no כוונה) from the wording of our משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's position that immersing for חולין does not need כוונה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's extra words 'והוחזק לחולין' suggest that the status of purity for חולין comes only when the person intended it. So כוונה is needed even for חולין.

steps.title: רב נחמן rereads the words 'was considered pure for חולין'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the משנה is not saying intention is needed for חולין. It is saying that even someone who did have intention for חולין still cannot eat מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: even though he took on pure status for חולין, he is still forbidden to eat מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבה's challenge by giving a different reading of the משנה's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה read 'was considered pure for חולין' as a requirement: you only get that status if you meant it. רב נחמן says the משנה is only describing a case. Even when a person did aim for חולין, that still does not help him for מעשר. So the משנה never says intention is needed for חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means. Used to give a new reading of a text.
He took on a pure status. He was treated as pure for a certain level.
Ordinary food that is not holy
Tithe. Produce that is holier and needs a higher level of purity.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
phrases.notes: רב נחמן is speaking here and explaining what our משנה really means.

phrases.english: Even though he took on pure status for non-holy food
he is forbidden to eat tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's challenge from Step 9
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Was considered pure for חולין' means that intention is required to become pure for חולין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words only describe a case. Even intention for חולין does not permit eating מעשר.

steps.title: רבה challenges again from 'as if he did not immerse'
steps.stepSummary: רבה quotes another line of the משנה: if a person immersed without taking on a status, it is as if he never immersed. That sounds like the immersion did nothing at all, even for חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה challenged him: if a person immersed but did not take on a pure status, it is as if he did not immerse. Doesn't that mean as if he did not immerse at all?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה brings a second line from our משנה to attack רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that immersing without taking on a status is 'as if he did not immerse.' If that means not at all, then the immersion did not even work for חולין. That would show intention is needed even for חולין, which goes against רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: He immersed in a מקוה
Is it not? Used to suggest that a text proves something.
At all

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
phrases.notes: רבה is challenging רב נחמן again.

phrases.english: If he immersed but did not take on pure status
it is as if he did not immerse.
Does it not mean
as if he did not immerse at all?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered, רבה brings a new challenge from the same משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that immersion for חולין works without intention
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'As if he did not immerse' sounds total. Without intention the immersion helps for nothing, even חולין.

steps.title: Only 'as if he did not immerse' for מעשר
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the משנה only means he is treated as not immersed for מעשר. For חולין his immersion still works.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means as if he did not immerse for מעשר, but he did immerse for חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן limits the משנה's words so they fit his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן says 'as if he did not immerse' is not total. It only applies to the higher level, מעשר, which does need intention. For חולין no intention is needed, so the immersion counts.

keyTerms.meaning: No. Here it rejects the suggested reading.
But

phrases.english: No, it means as if he did not immerse for tithe,
but he did immerse for non-holy food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's second challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the משנה's words
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'As if he did not immerse' means the immersion did nothing at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means not immersed for מעשר only. For חולין the immersion works.

steps.title: רבה finds a ברייתא that agrees with רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: רבה thought רב נחמן was only pushing off his proof. Then he looked into it and found a ברייתא that says it outright: without taking on a status, the person may not eat מעשר but may eat חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה thought רב נחמן was just pushing him off. He went out, looked carefully, and found a ברייתא: if a person immersed and did not take on a pure status, he is forbidden to eat מעשר and permitted to eat חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us that רב נחמן's answer was not just a way to escape. A ברייתא openly supports it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה thought רב נחמן's readings were only a way to show the משנה was not a clear proof. The ברייתא shows that רב נחמן's reading is the true הלכה. Without intention a person is pure for חולין but not for מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: He is just pushing him off. He gives a possible answer without really meaning it.
He went out and examined carefully
He found

steps.whatToRemember: Immersing without intention makes a person pure for חולין but not for מעשר. A ברייתא openly agrees with רב נחמן.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבה won here. In the end, the ברייתא he found supports רב נחמן.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רב נחמן's answers were the real meaning of the משנה, not just a debating move.

phrases.english: He thought
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבה.

phrases.english: that he was just pushing him off.
He went out, looked carefully, and found
that it was taught in a ברייתא:
If he immersed and did not take on pure status
he is forbidden to eat tithe
and permitted to eat non-holy food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms רב נחמן's answer from Step 12 with an outside source
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's view that intention is not needed for חולין, only for מעשר
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: טבל ולא הוחזק אסור למעשר ומותר לחולין

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: decide after coming up
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that a person who immersed and came up may then take on whatever level of purity he wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: if a person immersed and came up, he may take on pure status for whatever he wishes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching about when the intention for a level of purity has to happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now it sounded like intention had to happen during the immersion. רבי אלעזר says a person can decide after he comes out of the water. He can choose then to treat himself as pure for any level he wants.

keyTerms.meaning: He came up out of the water
He treats himself as pure. He takes on a pure status.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
If he immersed and came up
he may take on pure status
for whatever he wishes.
phrases.notes: He means that even after coming out of the water, he can choose which level of purity he is taking on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new teaching about the timing of intention for taking on a pure status
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After immersing and coming up, a person may take on pure status for any level he chooses.

steps.title: A ברייתא about one foot still in the water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא against רבי אלעזר. It says that while one foot is still in the water a person can raise his purity level, but once he has come up he can no longer take on a status.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection from a ברייתא: while one of his feet is still in the water, if he took on purity for a light matter, he may raise it to a severe matter. Once he has come up, he can no longer take on a status.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that seems to argue with רבי אלעזר. This step sets up the challenge, and the next line spells out the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר said a person may choose his level of purity after he comes up. The ברייתא says that only while a foot is still in the water can he move up from a light level to a severe one. Its last line, 'once he came up, he can no longer take on a status,' looks like a direct contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: While he is still (in the water)
He took on a status (decided what his טבילה is for)
A light matter, meaning a lower level of purity
A severe matter, meaning a higher level of purity

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
While one of his feet is still in the water,
if he took on a status for a light matter,
he may take on himself a status for a severe matter.
Once he came up, he can no longer take on a status.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict רבי אלעזר's statement in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's ruling that a person may choose his level of purity after coming up from the water.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says that once he comes up he can no longer take on a status, so choosing after coming up should not work.

steps.title: Reading the ברייתא as 'no status at all'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the problem: the ברייתא seems to mean that after coming up he cannot take on any status at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not saying that he cannot take on any status at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to the exact reading of the ברייתא that would disprove רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'he can no longer take on a status' means no status at all, then a person who immersed with no intention and came up is stuck. That directly opposes רבי אלעזר, who said he can choose whatever level he wants after coming up.

keyTerms.meaning: What, is it not...? (a way of suggesting a reading of a source)
He may not take on a status
At all

phrases.english: What, is it not saying
that he may not take on any status at all!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the reading of the ברייתא from step 15 that would contradict רבי אלעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ברייתא means no status at all after coming up, then choosing a level after coming up is impossible.

steps.title: The ברייתא only blocks changing a status already chosen
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: in the water he can always raise his level. After coming up, if he never chose a status he can still choose one, but if he already chose one he cannot change it.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. While he is still in the water, even if he already took on a status, he can take on a higher one. Once he has come up, if he did not take on any status, he can still take one on. But if he did take one on, he cannot take on another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the ברייתא more carefully, so it no longer argues with רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא was only talking about someone who already chose a light level. After coming up, his choice is locked in and he cannot upgrade it. Someone who chose nothing can still decide after coming up, which is exactly what רבי אלעזר said.

keyTerms.meaning: No (rejecting the suggested reading)
He came up (out of the water)
Even though

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that coming up out of the water ends the chance to choose. It only locks in a choice he already made. If he made no choice, he can still choose.

phrases.english: No:
while he is still in the water, even though he took on a status,
he may take on a status (a higher one).
Once he came up, if he had not taken on a status, he may take one on,
but if he had taken on a status, he may not take on another.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא עוֹדֵהוּ אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּחְזַק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading in step 16 and explains the ברייתא in a way that fits רבי אלעזר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the source: 'he cannot take on a status' only applies to someone who already chose a status.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: After coming up from the water, a person cannot take on any status at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: After coming up, a person who chose nothing can still choose. Only someone who already chose cannot change his choice.
steps.whatToRemember: In the water, you can always raise your level. Out of the water, you can still choose if you never chose, but a choice already made is locked in.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves רבי אלעזר's rule and shows that leaving the water only fixes an earlier choice in place.

steps.title: Which תנא holds that one foot in the water counts?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds the idea in the ברייתא that a person with one foot still in the water counts as still being in the מקוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who taught 'while one of his feet is still in the water'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks a side question about the ברייתא it just explained: whose opinion is it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats a person with only one foot in the water as still in the middle of his טבילה. Not everyone has to agree with that, so the גמרא wants to know which תנא holds it.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (which sage taught this)?
One of his feet
In the water

phrases.english: Who is the tanna who taught
'while one of his feet is still in the water'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תַּנָּא עוֹדֵהוּ רַגְלוֹ אַחַת בַּמַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from defending רבי אלעזר to asking who authored the ברייתא quoted in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a person with one foot still in the water is treated as still in the מקוה.

steps.title: רבי פדת says it is רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי פדת answers that the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי פדת said: it is רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי פדת answers the question: the ברייתא follows the view of רבי יהודה. The next step brings the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי פדת links the ברייתא to a known opinion of רבי יהודה. The proof that רבי יהודה holds this idea comes next from a משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is (the opinion of)

phrases.english: Rabbi Pedat said:
It is the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי פְּדָת רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.

steps.title: The משנה of two people in a מקוה of exactly forty סאה
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says that if two people immerse one after the other in a מקוה of exactly forty סאה, the second is impure. רבי יהודה says that if the first one's feet were still touching the water, the second is also pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: a מקוה was measured and had exactly forty סאה. Two people went down and immersed one after the other. The first is pure and the second is impure. רבי יהודה said: if the first one's feet were still touching the water, the second is also pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves רבי פדת's answer from a משנה, showing that רבי יהודה treats someone whose feet still touch the water as still in the מקוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the first person comes out, some water clings to him, so the מקוה drops below forty סאה and the second person's טבילה fails. רבי יהודה says that if the first person's feet are still in the water, that water still counts as part of the מקוה. So for רבי יהודה, a person partly in the water is still 'in' the מקוה, which is the idea behind the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: A ritual pool for טבילה
Forty סאה, the minimum amount of water a מקוה needs
Exactly (no more, no less)
They immersed

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יהודה, a person whose feet still touch the water still counts as in the מקוה. That is why the ברייתא about 'one foot still in the water' is his opinion.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
A ritual bath that was measured
and it holds exactly forty se'a,

phrases.aramaic: וְיָרְדוּ שְׁנַיִם וְטָבְלוּ זֶה אַחַר זֶה —
phrases.english: and two people went down and immersed one after the other:
the first is pure, and the second is impure.
phrases.notes: Water clings to the first person when he comes out, so the pool drops below forty סאה for the second.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיוּ רַגְלָיו שֶׁל רִאשׁוֹן נוֹגְעוֹת בַּמַּיִם —
phrases.english: If the feet of the first one were still touching the water,
the second is also pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that proves רבי פדת's claim in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה treats a person whose feet still touch the water as still in the מקוה, making him the author of the ברייתא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about two people immersing in a מקוה of exactly forty סאה, with רבי יהודה's view about the first person's feet.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the rule 'one foot in the water still counts' is not agreed by everyone; it comes from רבי יהודה's view.

steps.title: The argument is only about rabbinic extra-purity levels
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, says רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue only about מעלות דרבנן. For real impurity, everyone agrees the second person stays impure. This matches רבי פדת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: The argument is about the extra purity levels made by the Rabbis. But for going from real impurity to purity, everyone agrees the second person is impure as well. This fits what רבי פדת said.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא steps in to limit where the argument from the משנה (Step 20) applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's leniency (the first person's feet still touching the water) works only when the immersion is for a rabbinic extra purity level. For a real move from impurity to purity, even רבי יהודה agrees the second person is impure. So the ברייתא about a foot in the water follows only רבי יהודה, as רבי פדת said.

keyTerms.meaning: Extra levels of purity the Rabbis added (for example, to eat תרומה or קדשים)
Going from real impurity to purity
Everyone agrees
And this is the same as (this matches)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
The argument is about the extra purity levels of the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: The argument meant here is the one in the משנה from Step 20, between the חכמים and רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: but when going from impurity to purity,
everyone agrees the second person is impure as well.
And this is the view of Rabbi Pedat.
phrases.notes: רבי פדת said in Step 19 that only רבי יהודה holds that a foot in the water still counts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ מַחְלוֹקֶת בְּמַעֲלוֹת דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the argument in the משנה quoted in Step 20 to rabbinic purity levels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument applies only to מעלות דרבנן. For real impurity, all agree the second person is impure. This fits רבי פדת.

steps.title: Second version: the argument is only about real impurity
steps.stepSummary: A different version of רב נחמן's statement: the argument is only about going from real impurity to purity. For rabbinic extra levels, everyone agrees the second person is pure. This version disagrees with רבי פדת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it this way: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: The argument is about going from impurity to purity. But for the Rabbis' extra purity levels, everyone agrees the second person is pure as well. This disagrees with רבי פדת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, opposite version of רב נחמן's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the leniency is wider. For rabbinic purity levels, even the חכמים agree that a foot in the water still counts, so the second person is pure. That means the ברייתא about a foot in the water follows everyone, not only רבי יהודה, so it argues with רבי פדת.

keyTerms.meaning: And it disagrees

steps.confusionAlert: The two versions are opposites. In the first, the argument is about rabbinic levels and real impurity is strict for all. In the second, the argument is about real impurity and rabbinic levels are lenient for all.
steps.whatToRemember: Version 1 (argument about מעלות דרבנן) fits רבי פדת. Version 2 (argument about real impurity, while for מעלות all say pure) disagrees with רבי פדת.

phrases.english: There are those who say:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
The argument is about going from impurity to purity,
but with the extra purity levels of the Rabbis,
everyone agrees the second person is pure as well.
And this disagrees with Rabbi Pedat.
phrases.notes: If everyone agrees here, the ברייתא is not only רבי יהודה's view, which is what רבי פדת had said.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite version of the statement in Step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument applies only to real impurity. For מעלות דרבנן, all agree the second person is pure. This disagrees with רבי פדת.

steps.title: עולא asks about immersing needles on the first person's head
steps.stepSummary: עולא asked רבי יוחנן: according to רבי יהודה, can small utensils like needles be immersed on the head of the first person, whose foot is still in the water?
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: I asked רבי יוחנן: According to רבי יהודה, may one immerse needles and small tubes on the head of the first person?
steps.whatsHappening: עולא asks a new question built on רבי יהודה's view that a person with his feet still in the water counts as part of the מקוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first person still counts as connected to the מקוה, maybe his whole wet body counts as part of it. Then needles resting in the water on his head would be immersed, even though they are not in the pool itself.

keyTerms.meaning: I asked him
What is the law?
Needles
Small tubes or knitting needles

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר עוּלָּא, בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Ulla said: I asked Rabbi Yochanan:
According to Rabbi Yehuda, what is the law about immersing
needles and small tubes on the head of the first person?
phrases.notes: The 'first person' is the one from the משנה in Step 20, whose feet are still touching the water.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question based on רבי יהודה's view from Step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether, according to רבי יהודה, the first person's body counts as part of the מקוה, so that utensils on his head are immersed.

steps.title: The question depends on stretching down versus stretching up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the two sides of עולא's question: does רבי יהודה use only גוד אחית (the water on the person is seen as reaching down), or also גוד אסיק (the מקוה water is seen as reaching up to his head)?
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יהודה hold of 'stretch it down' but not 'stretch it up'? Or maybe he also holds of 'stretch it up'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out exactly what עולא's question depends on. The next step gives רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גוד אחית explains רבי יהודה in the משנה: the water on the first person counts as going down into the pool, so the pool stays at forty סאה. גוד אסיק would go further: the pool's water counts as reaching up to his head, so the needles there are immersed. The question is whether רבי יהודה accepts only the first idea or both.

keyTerms.meaning: Stretch it down: something above is treated as if it reaches down
Stretch it up: something below is treated as if it reaches up
Or perhaps
He holds of it / he does not hold of it

steps.whyThisMatters: It separates two different ideas inside רבי יהודה's view. Using one does not mean he must use the other.

phrases.aramaic: גּוּד אַחֵית אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Does Rabbi Yehuda hold of 'stretch it down,'
phrases.notes: 'Stretch it down' means the water on the person's body is seen as reaching down into the pool.

phrases.english: but not of 'stretch it up,'
phrases.notes: 'Stretch it up' would mean the pool's water is seen as reaching up to his head.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא: גּוּד אַסֵּיק נָמֵי אִית לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: or perhaps he holds of 'stretch it up' too?

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּד אַחֵית אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the two sides of עולא's question in Step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יהודה accepts only גוד אחית or also גוד אסיק.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן answers from the case of three pools in a stream
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings a source showing that רבי יהודה accepts גוד אסיק. רבי יהודה quotes רבי מאיר that you may immerse in the upper pool, because the middle pool's water is seen as rising up to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to עולא: You already learned this. There are three pools in a streambed: an upper one, a lower one, and a middle one. The upper and lower pools hold twenty סאה each, and the middle one holds forty סאה. A stream of rainwater flows between them. רבי יהודה says: מאיר used to say that one may immerse in the upper pool.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers עולא's question by pointing to a known teaching. In that teaching, רבי יהודה quotes a ruling that only works with גוד אסיק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The upper pool has only twenty סאה, which is not enough for a מקוה. It is still kosher because the forty סאה of the middle pool, which sits lower, is seen as reaching up to it through the rainwater (גוד אסיק). רבי יהודה repeats רבי מאיר's ruling without arguing, so he agrees with גוד אסיק. That means the needles could be immersed on the first person's head.

keyTerms.meaning: Shallow pools or dips in the ground that hold water
A stream or streambed
A measure of volume; a kosher מקוה needs forty of them
A thin stream of rainwater flowing down a slope
"Stretch it up": lower water is seen as reaching up to a higher place
One immerses (something or someone) to make it pure

steps.confusionAlert: The upper pool is not kosher by itself. It works only because the lower, bigger pool's water is seen as rising up to join it, and that is exactly the idea of גוד אסיק.
steps.whyThisMatters: If רבי יהודה accepts גוד אסיק, then the water of the מקוה can be seen as reaching up to the first person's head. That would let small utensils be immersed there, which answers עולא's question.

phrases.english: He said to him: You have already learned it:
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן is answering עולא, telling him the answer is in a teaching he already knows.

phrases.english: Three pools in a stream:
the upper one, the lower one, and the middle one;

phrases.aramaic: הָעֶלְיוֹנָה וְהַתַּחְתּוֹנָה שֶׁל עֶשְׂרִים עֶשְׂרִים סְאָה,
phrases.english: the upper and the lower ones hold twenty se'ah each,
and the middle one holds forty se'ah,
and a stream of rainwater passes between them,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: מֵאִיר הָיָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Meir used to say:
One may immerse in the upper one.
phrases.notes: The upper pool has only twenty סאה, so it works only if the middle pool's forty is seen as reaching up to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers עולא's question from steps 23-24 about whether רבי יהודה holds גוד אסיק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי יהודה accept גוד אסיק, so that utensils may be immersed on the first person's head?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. רבי יהודה quotes רבי מאיר, without disagreeing, that one may immerse in the upper 20-סאה pool. This only works with גוד אסיק.

steps.title: עולא begins a challenge from another teaching of רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a challenge to רבי יוחנן's proof by introducing a different ברייתא in רבי יהודה's name. The content continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting a challenge to רבי יוחנן's answer by bringing another teaching from רבי יהודה, and the actual words of that teaching come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וְהָתַנְיָא signals that a source is coming that seems to contradict what was just said. The challenge will suggest that רבי יהודה does not really hold like the ruling he quoted from רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a challenge against the proof רבי יוחנן brought in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's proof that רבי יהודה holds גוד אסיק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A different ברייתא in רבי יהודה's name seems to show that he does not agree with the ruling he quoted from רבי מאיר. The details follow in the next section.
